subject: psychology
title: Eyewitness Testimony: Anxiety
welcome_lead: Stress sharpens — or distorts — what we remember.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology EWT anxiety: weapon focus, Yerkes-Dodson, Yuille & Cutshall.
final_note: Anxiety is not simply bad for memory — context decides.

concepts.def: Emotional state of worry, raising arousal.
Attention drawn to weapon at expense of face.
Inverted-U: best performance at moderate arousal.
Vivid, lasting memory of shocking event (Brown & Kulik 1977).
Stress hormone affecting hippocampus and memory.

walkthroughs.body_html: Johnson & Scott (1976): participants overhearing a peaceful conversation saw a man emerge with a pen and grease (49% identification); those overhearing a heated argument saw him emerge with a knife and blood (33%). Weapons capture attention, reducing memory for faces.

13 witnesses to a real Vancouver shooting were re-interviewed 5 months later. Despite anxiety, they were highly accurate (80%+ correct details) and unaffected by leading questions. Real anxiety in real crimes may sharpen rather than impair memory.

The inverted-U law (originally 1908) predicts moderate arousal optimises recall. Deffenbacher (2004) meta-analysed 27 EWT anxiety studies and found high anxiety reduced accuracy in laboratory but not in real cases. Cortisol both consolidates (low dose) and impairs (high dose) memory via hippocampus.
